_comment: Karel Prometheus queries. All are INSTANT queries - the time-window work is
pushed into PromQL (max_over_time, predict_linear, increase, changes) rather
than pulling range data and reducing it in Python. That keeps the collector
trivial and lets Prometheus do what it is good at.
tier 1 = cheap and load-bearing, tier 2 = normal, tier 3 = expensive over
long windows. Same tier/budget semantics as the other collectors.

window_days: history the query genuinely needs. If Prometheus retention is shorter, the result is arithmetically meaningless and is suppressed rather than reported - a predict_linear over 14d computed from 30 minutes of data is not a forecast.

empty_means: 'none' for filtering expressions, where an empty result means nothing matched (good news). 'absent' where it means the metric is not scraped (a blind spot). Conflating them turns 'no node went NotReady' into 'we cannot see node readiness'.
source_job names the scrape job exporting the metrics a query needs, so a down target can be tied to the specific findings it blinds rather than reported as an unrelated fact.

queries.name: prom_up
queries._why: which scrape jobs exist at all

queries.name: prom_targets_down
queries._why: a down target is a monitoring blind spot, and Karel is the only thing that will tell you

queries.name: prom_retention_days
queries._why: how far back trend claims may legitimately reach

queries.name: node_mem_peak_7d
queries._why: MEASURED peak keyed by node name so it joins with the rest of the report; node_exporter series are keyed ip:port

queries.name: node_mem_working_set_peak_7d
queries._why: peak of what pods actually consumed, per node

queries.name: apiserver_5xx_rate_24h
queries._why: per-instance scraping makes this a real rate; the /metrics scrape could never do it

queries.name: etcd_db_predict_30d
queries._why: Prometheus does the regression; no two-point extrapolation

queries.name: etcd_db_size_now
queries._why: current db size: base of the compaction-aware quota math - the 30d prediction alone cannot say whether the quota is hit BEFORE the monthly compaction

queries.name: node_timex_offset_max
queries._why: the kernel's own clock-correction across nodes: a large offset means a clock being dragged - alert timelines, etcd and cert validity all assume aligned clocks

queries.name: etcd_leader_changes_24h
queries._why: the transient that daily snapshots cannot see at all

queries.name: pod_oomkills_24h
queries.expr: sum by (namespace, pod) (increase(kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total[24h]) > 0 and on(namespace, pod, container) (kube_pod_container_status_last_terminated_reason{reason="OOMKilled"} == 1))
queries._why: restarts whose last termination was OOMKilled; kube_pod_container_status_terminated_reason cannot do this - it is a gauge for the CURRENT terminated state whose series vanishes on restart, exactly when the kill becomes invisible, and increase() over it is 0 by construction

queries.name: node_notready_minutes_24h
queries._why: a node that flapped overnight and recovered; measured as per-node minutes with Ready!=true (a real zero per healthy node) instead of a filtered == 0, so all-Ready reports a 0 rather than vanishing into an ambiguous empty result

queries.name: pvc_used_pct_max
queries._why: PVC fullness is invisible from the Kubernetes API alone
